exact_theorem_extracted.definition_2_1: A_alpha := { arithmetic g : g(n) = O(n^{-alpha}) for each n }
exact_theorem_extracted.theorem_2_2: Suppose f in A_alpha and g in A_beta. Then, uniformly for all h with |h| <= x/2: sum_{H<=n<=x} F(n)G(n-h) = (x-H)*C(h) + O(E(x; alpha, beta)), where F = f*1, G = g*1, H = 1 if h<=0 else h, C(h) = sum_{a,b>=1, (a,b)|h} f(a)g(b)/[a,b], and the O-constant is ABSOLUTE.
exact_theorem_extracted.error_table_2_1: E(x;alpha,beta) = x^{1-alpha} if alpha<beta and alpha<1; x^{1-alpha} log x if alpha=beta<1; log x if 1=alpha<beta; log^2 x if alpha=beta=1; 1 if 1<alpha<beta.
exact_theorem_extracted.remark_2_4_product: If f,g multiplicative then C(h) = prod_p ( sum_{min{e1,e2} <= v_p(h)} f(p^e1) g(p^e2) / p^{max{e1,e2}} ).
exact_theorem_extracted.corollary_2_8: Paper explicitly instantiates G(n) = phi(n)/n and obtains prod_p (1-2/p^2) * prod_{p|h} (1 + 1/(p^3-2p)).
exact_theorem_extracted.partial_summation_extension: sum_{n<=x} Q(n)F(n)G(n-h) = C(h) int_1^x Q dt + Q(x)E(x;alpha,beta) + O(int_1^x |Q'(t)||E(t;alpha,beta)| dt), for Q differentiable with Q' bounded. This is what carries the linear n-weight from phi(n)/n back to phi(n).

step_1_membership.reason: |mu(d)/d| <= d^{-1}, so f(d) = O(d^{-1}), i.e. alpha = 1 exactly.
step_1_membership.identity: phi(n)/n = sum_{d|n} mu(d)/d = (mu(.)/. * 1)(n), so F = phi(n)/n has f = mu(.)/. and alpha = 1.

step_2_error_uniformity.claim: alpha = beta = 1 is inside the theorem's error table
step_2_error_uniformity.reason: E(x;1,1) = log^2 x. Uniform for all |h| <= x/2 with an ABSOLUTE O-constant. The paper's 'ease of exposition' text assumes 0<alpha<=beta<1, but the error table (2.1) explicitly covers alpha=beta=1.
step_2_error_uniformity.gate_resolved: RESOLVED BY AUTHORS, Section 3 opening, page 4, VERBATIM: 'The statements of the lemmas in this section hold true for all 0 < alpha <= beta. However, we restrict the proofs only to the case beta > alpha and alpha < 1. The proof works mutandis-mutandis for alpha >= 1 and the case beta = alpha will have an extra log factor.' Our case alpha = beta = 1 is covered on both counts: alpha >= 1 ('works mutatis mutandis') and beta = alpha ('extra log factor'). The extra log factor is EXACTLY why table (2.1) reads E(x;1,1) = log^2 x rather than the log x of the 1 = alpha < beta row. The authors' own remark explains the precise table entry the normalised totient requires.
step_2_error_uniformity.residual_formalisation_cost: The WRITTEN proofs of Lemmas 3.1-3.3 specialise to alpha < 1 (e.g. Lemma 3.3(a) uses 'For alpha < 1, this error is O(y^{1-alpha}/(jl)^{1-alpha})'). A Lean formalisation must redo roughly three lemmas at alpha = 1. The authors assert this is mutatis mutandis. That is ROUTINE re-derivation, not a missing theorem - a different category from every prior blocker in this programme.
step_2_error_uniformity.verdict: PASS - ALPHA=1 EXPLICITLY AUTHORISED BY THE AUTHORS

step_3_singular_series_derivation.derived: With f(1)=g(1)=1, f(p)=g(p)=-1/p, f(p^e)=0 for e>=2, Remark 2.4 gives local_p = 1 - 2/p^2 when p does not divide h, and 1 - 2/p^2 + 1/p^3 when p | h. Hence C(h) = prod_p(1-2/p^2) * prod_{p|h}(1 + 1/(p^3-2p)).
step_3_singular_series_derivation.validation: This reproduces the paper's own Corollary 2.8 constant EXACTLY, independently. A = prod_p(1-2/p^2) = 0.322634108930.

step_4_covariance_nondegeneracy.structural_finding: Cov(h) ALTERNATES SIGN BY PARITY OF h. Driven by the p=2 local factor 1 + 1/(2^3 - 2*2) = 1.25, which is the largest term in the product (5x the p=3 term 1/21). For a binary-expansion problem the covariance kernel's dominant mode is exactly mod 2.
step_4_covariance_nondegeneracy.quadratic_form: Q(lambda) = sum_{j,k} lambda_j lambda_k Cov(j-k) with the certificate's geometric weights lambda_j = 2^(L-1-j).
step_4_covariance_nondegeneracy.result: Q(lambda)/4^(L-1) converges to 0.031031532 > 0 (stable from L=20 through L=40). The certificate coefficient vector does NOT annihilate the non-trivial Ramanujan modes.
step_4_covariance_nondegeneracy.verdict: PASS - COVARIANCE NON-DEGENERATE WITH EXPLICIT CONSTANT

disconfirming_checks_specified_by_type_b.check_a_annihilation: 'if the certificate coefficient vector annihilates every non-trivial Ramanujan mode ... retire this composition' -> DID NOT FIRE. Q(lambda) -> 0.031031532 * 4^(L-1).
disconfirming_checks_specified_by_type_b.check_b_error_vs_band: 'if the proven error is larger than the separation band ... retire' -> DID NOT FIRE at the second-moment scale. After partial summation with the n-weight the error is O(x^2 log^2 x) against a main term of order x^3 * C(h); the lambda's factor out of both sides, leaving x >> log^2 x.
